analysis.title: UL Solutions (ULS): 3Q beat-and-raise supported by volume-led growth, record margins and improving visibility into 2027
key_insights: ULS reported 3Q26 revenue of $823mn, up 5.1% y/y, above GS estimate of 4.4% and FactSet consensus of 4.2%. Organic revenue grew 7.0% y/y vs GS 6.1% and consensus 5.3%, accelerating from 6.6% in 2Q.

Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 bps y/y to 28.6%, vs GS forecast 27.8% and consensus 28.3%, driven by operating leverage and productivity gains in Industrial and Consumer. Adjusted EPS was $0.62 vs GS and consensus of $0.61.

GS says the results raise confidence that ULS can sustain at least mid-single-digit organic growth into 2027, supported by volume-led certification demand and order growth outpacing revenue growth in energy transition, electrification and materials.
Industrial organic revenue grew 8.4% y/y (about 9% excluding Advisory), driven by energy, automation and materials. Industrial EBITDA margin rose 150 bps y/y to a record 36.1%.

Certification testing revenue rose nearly 11% y/y, which ULS identifies as the best proxy for data center activity, and growth was primarily volume-driven. Successive server and chipset generations require added testing across power distribution, power conversion and liquid cooling, supporting a multiyear opportunity.
Consumer organic revenue grew 5.9% y/y despite a ~150 bps headwind from planned business exits (about 7.4% excluding exits). Consumer EBITDA margin rose 170 bps to a record 21.4%.

The Eurofins E&E acquisition closed October 1 and should add ~$50mn of revenue in 4Q. It adds lab and engineering capability in Europe and Asia, particularly Korea. Go-to-market and lab utilization synergies are largely expected by end of 2028.

Risk & Compliance Software organic revenue rose 4.7% y/y, but segment EBITDA margin fell 1,080 bps y/y to 18.9% on the EHS divestiture, negative operating leverage on a smaller revenue base and transaction costs. ULS expects improvement in 4Q but gave limited specificity on the pace of recovery.

Advisory revenue was relatively flat y/y and remains a drag on Industrial growth. US renewable energy and commercial real estate are headwinds, partly offset by stronger project activity in Europe, particularly Germany.

ULS raised FY26 organic revenue growth guidance from mid-single-digits to ~6.5% (including a 70 bps reduction from business exits) and kept the ~27.0% EBITDA margin outlook. About 200 bps of underlying margin expansion is offset by ~90 bps of incremental E&E transaction and integration costs. 4Q integration costs are running above earlier assumptions and will continue into 2027.

GS raised 2026/27/28 revenue estimates to $3,277mn/$3,654mn/$3,927mn from $3,221mn/$3,429mn/$3,682mn, mainly for the E&E acquisition. EBITDA margin forecasts are kept at 27.0%/27.5%/28.0%. EPS estimates move to $2.27/$2.69/$3.04 from $2.31/$2.61/$2.94.

GS maintains Neutral and raises the 12-month price target to $88 from $86. The target uses 16.75x (down from 17.50x) rolled-forward NTM+1YR EBITDA of $1,077mn, lowered for reduced near-term margin visibility. It sits at a premium to the 12.5x European TIC peer median.

market_movers.rationale: GS raised the target to $88 from $86 and kept Neutral, with 9.5% upside to the $80.40 price. Valuation is seen as balancing durable organic growth and margin potential against integration costs, Advisory headwinds and weak Risk & Compliance Software margins.

earnings_insights: ULS 3Q26 (reported 11/3/2026): revenue $823mn, +5.1% y/y reported vs GS est 4.4% and FactSet consensus 4.2%. Organic +7.0% vs GS est 6.1% and consensus 5.3%.
ULS 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA $235mn, margin 28.6% vs GS est 27.8% and FactSet consensus 28.3%. Adjusted EPS $0.62 reported vs GS est $0.61 and consensus $0.61. GAAP EPS $0.53 vs GS est $0.54.

ULS FY26 guidance: organic revenue growth raised to ~6.5% from mid-single-digits (includes 70 bps drag from business exits). EBITDA margin reiterated at ~27.0%. GS says guidance points to positive consensus revisions for revenue and stable revisions for EBITDA margin.

Pre-print GS FY26 estimates were revenue $3,221mn, EBITDA $870mn (27.0% margin), EPS $2.31. FactSet consensus was revenue $3,218mn, EBITDA $878mn (27.3% margin), EPS $2.32. New GS FY26 estimates: revenue $3,277mn, EBITDA $883mn, adjusted EPS $2.27.
GS 4Q26E: revenue $880mn (up from $830mn prior), adjusted EBITDA $232mn at 26.4% margin, adjusted EPS $0.56 (down from $0.61 prior) reflecting E&E integration costs and a higher tax rate.
risk_factors: Downside risks: macro and geopolitical uncertainty, premium pricing relative to competitors, elevated growth investment that could limit margin expansion, and FX.
Upside risks: faster product innovation, returns on recent lab and testing site investments, regulatory actions imposing stricter safety standards, M&A, and efficiency gains at testing facilities.
Muted Advisory trends could limit Industrial growth, and depressed Risk & Compliance Software margins plus elevated E&E integration costs will likely constrain 2027 margin expansion.

tension_points.bull_case: Operating leverage, productivity, AI-enabled processes, better lab utilization and value-based pricing support sustained EBITDA margin expansion. Industrial and Consumer margins hit records, and most efficiency program benefits are captured.
tension_points.bear_case: Depressed Risk & Compliance Software margins (18.9%) and elevated E&E integration costs, with 4Q costs above earlier assumptions and more in 2027, will likely constrain 2027 margin expansion. Advisory is flat.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Remaining headcount actions are expected to finish by end of 1Q 2027, and ULS expects Risk & Compliance Software to return toward pre-divestiture margin ranges after 4Q. Failure to improve in 4Q would weaken the margin case.
